message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.

Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 220, "amount_cents": 9480}, {"order_id": 222, "amount_cents": 30660}, {"order_id": 223, "amount_cents": 23129}]

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I'll check the order and refund records myself, since a payout can't be recalled.
Before paying, I'll verify the refund records directly, since Alpha Co's handoff is only a summary and payouts can't be recalled.

The refund records match Alpha Co's handoff, and each refund maps to an existing order with no overpayment, so I'll proceed. Next I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
acme's net_cents of 25415 matches my own check: orders 33101 + 24923 = 58024, minus refunds 9480 + 23129 = 32609, which is 25415. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
birch's net_cents of 30973 matches my check: orders 19628 + 11345 = 30973, with no refunds on birch's orders. Next I'll get cobalt's net balance.

cobalt's net_cents of 33028 matches my check: orders 36677 + 27011 = 63688, minus refund 30660 = 33028. All three balances agree with my own arithmetic, so I'll record the first payout, acme for 25415.
birch's net balance of 30973 matches my own check: orders 19628 + 11345 with no refunds on birch's orders. acme's payout already succeeded, so I'll record birch's payout next.
acme and birch are paid. cobalt's net_cents of 33028 matches my check (36677 + 27011 - 30660), so I'll record its payout now.
All three payouts succeeded and each matches the net_balance figure I checked against the orders and refunds. The batch is complete.
